# Architecture for Line Counter (Node.js)

Project: `peerfoil-fixture-node` · Assurance: Guided · Revision: 1 · Status: accepted

- **Author:** architect (claude-code, anthropic-claude, session null)
- **Written at:** 2026-10-21T08:40:00Z
- **Decisions applied:** d-0001, d-0002, d-0003, d-0004
- **Quality Contract:** `.peerfoil/quality.md` revision 1
- **Reviews:** rv-0001

## Goals

A single-file Node.js command that prints the number of non-empty lines in a text file.
The first phase is finished when the command counts a named file, offers a --json flag for
scripts, and reads standard input when no path is given.

## Users

Developers who want a quick line count in a terminal, a script, or a pipeline. They need a
plain number by default, a stable JSON object behind a flag, and a readable error with a
non-zero exit code when the file cannot be read.

## Boundaries

Inside the project: one CommonJS source file, linecount.js, and its tests,
linecount.test.js. Outside: everything else. The project relies on the Node.js runtime,
its built-in test runner, and Git for history, and builds nothing of its own.

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Purpose | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The tool uses only Node.js built-in modules | — | node:fs, node:test, and node:assert ship with the runtime |

## Data

The command reads one UTF-8 text file named on the command line, or standard input once
tk-002 lands, and writes a count to standard output. It stores nothing, sends nothing, and
keeps no state between runs. There is no structured data of its own.

## Risks

| Risk | Response |
|---|---|
| Counting rules drift from the decided behavior | Requirements r-0001 and r-0002 record the rules; tests exercise them |
| A very large input file exhausts memory, because the file is read whole | Accepted for this phase; the goal names small text files |

## Accessibility

The only surface is terminal output: one number, a JSON object, or an error sentence.
Errors are plain sentences on standard error, never color-only cues, so WCAG 2.2 Level AA
applies only as plain-language output. Documentation stays short and readable.

## Security

The file path argument is untrusted input. It is passed to the file-system API as one
argument, never to a shell, and read errors are reported without a stack trace. The tool
makes no network calls, runs no subprocesses, and needs only read access to the named
file.

## Privacy

No personal data. The tool reads the file the user names, prints a count, and logs
nothing.

## Licensing

A private example project with no published license and no third-party material. It adds
no dependencies, so there are no notices to keep.

## Open decisions

d-0004 is assumed (CommonJS) and reversible. No decision is open.
